prompt_title: Delegating thread safety to a ConcurrentHashMap. M1
prompt_content:
Please write a concurrent program in Java 8 that implements the following functionality: Create a Java class called MysticBeastTracker that orchestrates the perches of sky-beasts in a thread-safe dreamscape. The class should use a ConcurrentHashMap to store beast perches, where each beast is marked by a unique String sigil and its current perch is represented by a Glyph object. Provide the following functionality: 
A constructor that welcomes an initial Map of beast sigils to Glyphs and imbues the internal concurrent map with these values. 
A method getPerches() that reveals an unmodifiable view of the current beast perches to prevent external tinkering. 
A method getPerch(String sigil) that displays the current perch of the specified beast or null if the beast does not exist. 
A method setPerch(String sigil, int spark, int glimmer) that transmutes the perch of an existing beast with the given sigil to the new coordinates (spark, glimmer). If the beast does not exist, this method should evoke an appropriate exception such as IllegalArgumentException. 
An alternative method getPerchesAsStatic() that captures a snapshot of the current perches as an unmodifiable Map to provide a consistent view of all perches at the moment of invocation. 
Ensure that all operations are thread-safe without requiring additional synchronization in the class. Use standard Java libraries for concurrency and collections. The requirements are as follows:

All classes and methods must be defined within a single .java file;
The program must include a public static void main(String[] args) method as the entry point;
No external libraries or dependencies should be used;
The code should be clear, well-structured, and follow Java 8 syntax standards;
If multiple classes are needed, they should all be placed in the same file, with non-public classes defined using the class keyword. 
The implementation must use multithreading to perform tasks concurrently. You may use Thread, Runnable, or ExecutorService from the standard Java library to achieve this. Ensure that thread safety is considered where necessary. 
Write Java 8 code only. Output a single complete code block using ```java```. Do not include any explanations, comments, or extra text. Only output the code, nothing else.
The total number of threads used in the program, including the main thread, must not exceed 6. Use a fixed thread pool or manually manage at most 5 additional threads beyond the main thread. Avoid unbounded thread creation or cached thread pools.

Please write a concurrent program in Java 8 that implements the following functionality: Write a Java class called SimulatedCAS that simulates the behavior of a Compare-and-Swap (CAS) operation, which is commonly used in concurrent programming for atomic updates. The class should maintain an internal integer value and provide thread-safe methods to interact with it.

The class should include:

A private integer field value to store the current value.
A synchronized get() method that returns the current value.
A synchronized compareAndSwap(int expectedValue, int newValue) method that checks if the current value matches the expectedValue. If it does, it updates the value to newValue; otherwise, it leaves the value unchanged. This method should return the original (old) value before any potential update.
A synchronized compareAndSet(int expectedValue, int newValue) method that uses compareAndSwap() to determine whether the value was successfully updated. It should return true if the value was changed (i.e., if the old value matched the expected value), and false otherwise.
Ensure that all methods are thread-safe using the synchronized keyword to prevent race conditions when accessed by multiple threads concurrently. The requirements are as follows:

All classes and methods must be defined within a single .java file;
The program must include a public static void main(String[] args) method as the entry point;
No external libraries or dependencies should be used;
The code should be clear, well-structured, and follow Java 8 syntax standards;
If multiple classes are needed, they should all be placed in the same file, with non-public classes defined using the class keyword. 
The implementation must use multithreading to perform tasks concurrently. You may use Thread, Runnable, or ExecutorService from the standard Java library to achieve this. Ensure that thread safety is considered where necessary.

Do not add any annotations.

The class should include:

A method ProductInfo loadProductInfo() which simulates loading data and may throw a custom exception called DataLoadException.
A FutureTask that wraps a Callable to execute the loadProductInfo method in the background.
A dedicated Thread instance to run the FutureTask.
A start() method to begin the execution of the background task.
A get() method that returns the loaded ProductInfo and propagates any exceptions thrown during the loading process, including properly handling and rethrowing them (e.g., wrapping unexpected exceptions using a utility-like approach).

An interface ProductInfo as a placeholder for the loaded data type.
A custom exception class DataLoadException that extends Exception.

Define a PrimeProducer class that extends Thread.
The producer should generate 2 prime numbers and put them into the queue.
It should stop when it has produced the requested number of primes or if interrupted.
A consumer thread should read from the same queue, print each prime number as it is consumed, and stop after processing all generated primes.
The main method should start both threads, wait for the consumer to finish, then signal the producer to stop and wait for it to finish.
Use proper error handling for interruptions.
Make sure the code is thread-safe and uses Java 8 features appropriately." 
Ensure proper handling of thread interruption to allow clean termination. The requirements are as follows:

All classes and methods must be defined within a single .java file;
The program must include a public static void main(String[] args) method as the entry point;
No external libraries or dependencies should be used;
The code should be clear, well-structured, and follow Java 8 syntax standards;
If multiple classes are needed, they should all be placed in the same file, with non-public classes defined using the class keyword. 
The implementation must use multithreading to perform tasks concurrently. You may use Thread, Runnable, or ExecutorService from the standard Java library to achieve this. Ensure that thread safety is considered where necessary. 
Write Java 8 code only. Output a single complete code block using ```java```. Do not include any explanations, comments, or extra text. Only output the code, nothing else. 
The total number of threads used in the program, including the main thread, must not exceed 3. Use a fixed thread pool or manually manage at most 2 additional threads beyond the main thread. Avoid unbounded thread creation or cached thread pools. 
Do not add any annotations.
